performers: Alisa Weilerstein, cello; Jason Yoder, piano
question: How do the sustained cello and repeated piano attacks share a phrase?
intro: Alisa Weilerstein and Jason Yoder performed Le Cygne at the White House’s Evening of Classical Music on 4 November 2009. The cello sustains the melody above piano figuration; the source is the audio from the official video.

cues.title: Two different kinds of sustain
cues.text: Weilerstein’s cello sustains the tune while Yoder’s piano renews the accompaniment through separate attacks. Listen for how they join a phrase despite those different ways of producing sound.
cues.evidence: Commons identifies both performers and instruments; the written melody and broken-chord accompaniment are described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_cygne. This concerns the whole performance, not an exact entrance at zero.

cues.title: An early crest
cues.text: In this early stretch, the phrase grows and then releases into quieter sound. Follow the cello line through the change rather than expecting the accompaniment to stop.
cues.evidence: The report’s strongest boundary is at 0:38. Relative level reaches −15.0 dB at 0:45 and drops to −24.6 dB at 0:50; the report measures the combined instruments.

cues.title: Two middle swells
cues.text: The middle passage has successive rises separated by a relaxation. Compare the lengths of those gestures while keeping the long cello melody in mind.
cues.evidence: The 1:15 and 1:25 windows are among the five highest; the 1:20 window between them is lower. Boundaries at 1:12 and 1:28 support passage-level placement.

cues.title: The later broad rise
cues.text: A later swell grows out of quieter playing, then recedes towards the close. Keep following both the sustained line and the piano’s moving accompaniment across the crest.
cues.evidence: Relative level rises from −25.2 dB at 1:35 to −9.7 dB at 1:50, the report’s highest five-second window, then falls to −28.1 dB at 2:05.

cues.title: The musical close
cues.text: The closing phrase becomes quieter before the remaining piano sound is released. This live source continues beyond the music, so its complete file length is not the duration of the phrase.
cues.evidence: The 2:15–2:20 windows are quiet; the timbre changes sharply at the 2:36 boundary, with brightness rising above 2200 Hz. The comparison stops at 155 seconds, before this post-performance sound; the final ten seconds are silent.

transitions.title: The continuing phrase gains weight
transitions.how: The same cello-and-piano texture develops a stronger phrase contour. The marker locates a measured change before the middle swells rather than a precisely aligned change of theme.
transitions.evidence: Boundary at 1:02 precedes the 1:15 and 1:25 high-level windows. Instrumentation is documented by the recording source.

transitions.title: The middle swells retreat
transitions.how: The middle swells subside into a quieter melodic span. A new rise follows without replacing the cello-and-piano texture.
transitions.evidence: Boundary at 1:32; relative level falls from −12.5 dB at 1:25 to −25.2 dB at 1:35.

transitions.title: The later swell becomes a release
transitions.how: The later crest recedes towards the last phrase. Listen for the difference between the melodic release and the piano resonance that continues around it.
transitions.evidence: Boundaries at 2:00 and 2:04 accompany the fall from the 1:50 high point to the quiet 2:15–2:20 windows; an exact release is not located.
